title: Web3 Splitter: split token payments by percentage (and learn PDA signing from two real bugs)
summary: Create a vault that splits any SPL token between wallets by percentage. Then see, on devnet, why its claim only works for the creator.
what: Web3 Splitter lets you create a named **splitter vault** for one SPL token and a list of recipients with percentages that must add up to 100. Anyone who deposits tokens into it has the amount booked to each recipient by percentage, and each recipient can **claim** their share. The tokens sit in a token account owned by a PDA, so only the program can move them. Running it on devnet exposed two real bugs in the fork's `claim`: it signs with the wrong seeds, and it pays out the whole vault. This lesson uses them to show exactly how PDA signing works.
app_note: The fork's own Vue 3 + Vite app (`src/`), unchanged apart from this devnet program ID and its IDL, the base path, and hash routing (`#/create`, `#/action`, `#/list`) for static hosting.

try_steps.do: You need a devnet SPL token. With the Solana CLI set to devnet and your Phantom keypair (or any funded keypair): `spl-token create-token`, then `spl-token create-account <MINT>` and `spl-token mint <MINT> 1000`. Then `spl-token transfer <MINT> 100 <your Phantom address> --fund-recipient` if you minted from another keypair.
try_steps.see: Your wallet holds a token you control. Copy its mint address.

try_steps.do: Open [the Create page](/dapps/web3-splitter/#/create) and connect with **Select Wallet**.
try_steps.see: "Craete New Splitter" (sic) with Splitter Name, Token address and Add Address fields.

try_steps.do: Type a short name, paste the mint into **Token address**. In **Add Address** replace the pre-filled address with **your own** wallet address, keep `100` %, and press the **+** button. Press **Create** and approve.
try_steps.see: An `initialize` transaction. It creates the vault PDA and the vault's token account. (Make yourself the only recipient for now: see step 6 for why.)

try_steps.do: Open [the List page](/dapps/web3-splitter/#/list) and copy your vault's address.
try_steps.see: All vaults of the program, read with `program.account.vault.all()`.

try_steps.do: Open [the Actions page](/dapps/web3-splitter/#/action), paste the vault address, press **Get it**. Enter `25` in the deposit field and press **Deposite**; approve.
try_steps.see: A `deposite` transaction: 25 tokens move from your token account into the vault's. The table lists your wallet with Share 100 %. (The balance column assumes 9 decimals and may show a wrong number or NaN.)

try_steps.do: Press **Claim** on your row and approve.
try_steps.see: A `claim` transaction: the 25 tokens come back to you. Now repeat steps 3–6 with **two** recipients, 60 % you and 40 % a second wallet, and try Claim from the second wallet: it fails. Section 4 explains why.

instructions.name: `initialize`: create the vault
steps: It sums `percentages` and fails with `Unauthorized` unless the total is exactly 100 (our test with a total of 90 was rejected).
It also fails unless there is one percentage per recipient (rejected in our test with 1 percentage for 2 recipients).
`seeds = ["vault", name_seed(&name), authority, token]`: the same creator can have one vault per name per token. `name_seed` cuts the name to 32 bytes because a single seed can't be longer.
`associated_token::authority = vault` creates the vault's token account **owned by the PDA**. That is the only place tokens are held.

instructions.name: `deposite`: book shares and move tokens in
steps: `total += amount`, then for each recipient `booked[i] += pct[i] × amount / 100` (integer division, so tiny remainders are not booked).
A token `transfer` CPI from the depositor's token account to the vault's, authorised by the depositor's signature.

Note what is **not** checked in `Deposite` (lines 256–275): the vault and `vault_token_account` have no seeds or address constraints, so the program trusts the client to pass the vault's real token account.

instructions.name: `claim`: pay a recipient, signed by the PDA

refs.note: access control: claimer must be a recipient

steps: Access control: the claimer must be in `vault.accounts`, else `Unauthorized` (a stranger's claim was rejected in our test).
It finds the claimer's row and its booked amount `money`.

To move tokens out of an account owned by a PDA, the program calls `transfer` with `new_with_signer(seeds)`. The runtime re-derives an address from those seeds and the program ID; if it equals the authority of the token account, the transfer is signed.

Bug 1 (line 182): the seeds use `claimer` where the vault was created with `authority`. For anyone but the creator, the derived address is not the vault, and the transfer fails: our recipient-B claim failed with "Could not create program address with signer seeds".
Bug 2 (line 195): it transfers `vault_balance` (the whole vault total) instead of `money`. Our authority, booked for 60, received all 100 tokens.

instructions.name: `update` and `delete` (authority only)
steps: `has_one = authority @ WrongOwner` and the `access_control` check refuse anyone but the creator (both rejections are in Proof).
`update` replaces the percentages for **future** deposits; amounts already booked stay as they were ([60, 40] stayed after updating to 70/30).
`delete` closes the Vault account and returns its rent. Despite the comment, it does not move any tokens out of the vault's token account.

innovation.title: a PDA that owns a token account, and signs with seeds
innovation.text: The vault's tokens are held in an associated token account whose owner is the Vault PDA. A PDA has no private key, so nobody can sign for it, except the program, by passing the exact seeds (plus bump) that produce that address to `CpiContext::new_with_signer`. That is what makes a trustless vault possible. And it is exactly what this fork gets wrong: the seeds must be the ones used at creation.
more: Put the two excerpts side by side: `authority.to_account_info().key` at creation vs `ctx.accounts.claimer.key()` at claim. When claimer == authority they produce the same address and claim works (our UI run and the 60/40 script). For anyone else they don't, and the runtime refuses to sign.
The fix is one line: use the stored `vault.authority` in the claim seeds, and transfer `money`, not `vault_balance`. That is Exercise 1.

frontend.title: Create: derive the vault PDA and its token account in the browser
steps: `handlePDA` uses the same seeds as the program: `"vault"`, the name, the wallet, the mint.
`findAssociatedTokenAddress(PDA, mint)` computes the vault's token account; `initialize(...)` passes both and Anchor creates them.

frontend.title: Deposit: amount × 10^decimals
steps: It reads the mint's `decimals` with `getMint` and sends `amount × 10^decimals` base units, with `accountsStrict` listing every account.

frontend.title: Claim
steps: The claimer's token account is its ATA for the mint (the program creates it with `init_if_needed` if missing). The Claim button only appears on the row whose address equals the connected wallet.

exercises.title: Fix claim and prove it on a local validator
steps: Clone the fork at `ced1cca` and open `splitterprogram/programs/splitterprogram/src/lib.rs`.
Line 182: replace `&ctx.accounts.claimer.key().to_bytes()` with `vault.authority.as_ref()`.
Line 195: replace `vault_balance` with `money`.
`anchor build`, `anchor test`, with a 60/40 vault, a deposit of 100, and claims from both recipients.
exercises.expect: Recipient B's claim now succeeds and receives 40; the authority receives 60; the vault ends at 0.

exercises.title: Watch the seeds error yourself
steps: Create a 60/40 vault on the live app with a second wallet as the 40 % recipient, deposit, then press Claim from the second wallet.
exercises.expect: The transaction fails; in the error logs: "Could not create program address with signer seeds" (as recorded in Proof).

exercises.title: Check the 100 % rule
steps: On the Create page, the + button won't let the total pass 100. From a script, call `initialize` with percentages [50, 40].
exercises.expect: Rejected with `Unauthorized` (the program's own check, independent of the UI).

exercises.title: Long names
steps: Compare `name_seed` (program, line 389) with `handlePDA` in `src/lib/useWorkspace.ts`.
Create a vault whose name is 40 characters long.
exercises.expect: The program would accept it (it truncates the seed to 32 bytes), but the app passes the full name to `findProgramAddressSync`, which throws "Max seed length exceeded" in the browser, so nothing is sent. Truncating the name to 32 bytes in `handlePDA` fixes it.

exercises.title: Lock down deposits
steps: In `Deposite`, add `constraint = vault_token_account.key() == vault.vault_token_account` to `vault_token_account`.
Rebuild and call `deposite` passing a token account that is not the vault's.
exercises.expect: Rejected with a constraint error; deposits can no longer book shares without paying the real vault.
